with.line: Another one off the wreck! Over here, by the fire.

script.text: You're awake. Good. Sit up slow, the sand moves under you. Eat this first, talk after.

then.text: Rune Isle. Your ship struck the rocks under the lighthouse, same as all of them. I watched it come in on the night tide.

You're not the first, and you won't be the last. A ship comes in every few weeks. Something out there pulls them. The current runs wrong, the wind swings round, and every helm ends up pointed at that light.
Crews fight it all night and wake up here anyway. Only ones like you walk off the wrecks. Don't ask me why. I stopped asking.
North. Take the road up between the hills. The camp's at the top: a fire, a pub, a few tents, and people. Ifeoma cooks, Idris buys skins, Runa keeps the rats off. That's where you trade, not here.
Rats on the way, a snake or two, nothing worse. Keep something in your hand and you'll be fine.

Past the camp the island opens up. There are two towns worth the walk. The druids' town, round the rune temple, where they still carve. And the warriors' town to the east, where they won't touch a rune.
They don't love each other. My brother lives with the warriors. Go and see both, then pick.
You've had your free one. The rest you buy up at the camp. Ifeoma cooks, and she'll take what you hunt off you too.

else.text: Listen, because this matters. Food is what mends you here. Hungry, you stay hurt. Fed, you heal. Nothing else does it.

traded.text: Eat it now, not later. You'll feel it close you up.

cancel.text: It'll be here. Don't go far without eating.

then.text: Not the way you mean. Nobody does, here. You go under, you wake up, and it hurts, and you've lost something. Like the tide taking a bit of the beach.
Usually something small. Forty-odd times for me. Wolves I can live with. Anyone tells you a troll is not so bad, they've not met one.
It's been like this since the night the light changed. A hundred and thirty years, near enough. Nobody's aged a day since. Nobody's stayed dead.
Look at the top of the lighthouse after dark. That's not oil burning. The man who built it carved runes, and the stone did what he told it. That night he went up to the top, and he never came down.
Whatever stopped us dying, it started up there. Leave it be for now. You're not ready for that climb.
Tove. I hunt. Born here, when the island had a harbour and people still got old. I threw harpoons off a whaleboat then. I couldn't tell you how now.
The light out there brought your ship in. Halvard built it to bring ships home. It still brings them. Just not home.
Eat before you're hungry, not after.

with.line: Five skins for a cap! Boots before anything else!

script.text: Skins, {partner}? Good, good. Leather for leather, that's how I sell, my friend. You bring the hide, I bring the needle, and we both go home happy.

then.text: Caps and helms. Every one of them starts as a skin, my friend. The iron is only riveted onto my leather, so you pay for my leather first.
{item:leather-cap}. One point, five skins. The cheapest thing I sell, and still better than nothing on your head.

traded.text: Better than your hair, eh? What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:iron-helm}. Two points, and two more against blunt. Five skins and thirty gold, and you'll thank me the first time a club finds your head.

traded.text: That is what a helm is for, my friend. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:knights-helm}. Three points, and three more against sharp blows. Fifty gold. I don't sell many, so I don't drop the price.

traded.text: You'll see less and live longer. A good trade. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:wolfskin-hood}. One point, and three against sharp blows. Three wolf skins: the wolves pay for their own hoods. I like that.

traded.text: Wear it with the ears up. The wolves hate it. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: As you like, as you like. What else?
Only one coat on my rack, my friend. The armourer in the warriors' town has the rest. Tell her Idris sent you; she'll charge you more for it.
{item:wolfskin-coat}. Two points, and five against sharp blows. Five wolf skins and forty gold. Count them: five.

traded.text: A wolf could not bite through it. I've watched one try. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: As you like, as you like. What else?
Boots! Now we are talking. A good sole is a good hide, and I have the hides. Wolves go for the legs, remember.
{item:worn-boots}. One point, five skins, and soft enough to walk in on the first day. No blisters, or your skins back. Almost.

traded.text: They'll do. Better than sand between your toes. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:hobnailed-boots}. One point, and three against blunt. The nails come from Wenna, so the price is the price.

traded.text: Nailed through. You'll hear yourself coming. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:steel-sabatons}. Two points, and two against sharp blows. Steel toes on my soles. Heavy, yes, yes.

traded.text: Heavy, and worth it. Lift your knees. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: {item:wolfskin-boots}. One point, and three against sharp blows. Three wolf skins and twenty gold.

traded.text: Quiet on the floor. Even Tove won't hear you. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: Fair enough, fair enough. What else?
{item:leather-backpack}. Eight more things carried, on your back where your hands stay free. Fifteen skins, I know, I know. Count the stitches and tell me it's too much.

traded.text: Fill it, then come back and sell me what's in it. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. It will wait for you. Anything else?

then.text: Selling? Better still. I pay gold for anything you cut off a beast. Show me, show me.
2 gold for each {item:skin}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 3 gold for each {item:wolf-skin}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold for each {item:bone}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold for each {item:rat-tail}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold for each {item:bat-wing}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold for each {item:rabbit-foot}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 5 gold for each {item:bear-claw}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 6 gold for each {item:troll-tusk}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold for each {item:yeti-fur}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: 25 gold for each {item:cyclops-eye}, my friend. Count them out, and I'll count them again.

traded.text: Counted, and paid. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. My price doesn't go up while you wait. Anything else?

then.text: As you like, as you like. What else?
Idris Kaya, saddler. I came on a trading ship and stayed for a woman, who did not stay for me. No horses after the harbour went, so now I make boots and jerkins.
Six deaths in a hundred and thirty years. Six! Four wolves, a fall, a snake. That's a good record here, my friend. Ask Tove hers.
Remember: wolves go for the legs first. Boots before anything else. And bring me skins!

with.line: Stew's hot! Sit, eat!

script.text: Sit, sit. Eat. You look like the sea chewed you and spat you out, o. Mind the pot, it's hot.

then.text: Two gold a loaf. Pell bakes better in the town, but my bread is here and his is not.

traded.text: Eat it warm, my dear. Cold bread is a sadness. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, o. Anything else?

then.text: Three gold. Off the fire just now. Blow on it first, you hear?

traded.text: There. Eat it before Tove sees it. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, o. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold a piece. It comes from the warriors' town, and it smells like it.

traded.text: There. Eat it before Tove sees it. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, o. Anything else?

then.text: Bring me meat and I will pay you. One gold a cut. Bring me rats and Biscuit will pay you back, ehn?

traded.text: Good meat. This one goes in the pot tonight. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, o. Anything else?

then.text: Me? Ifeoma. I ran the busiest eating house on the harbour, before the flood took it. Sailors from ten countries, all shouting for my pepper soup. Now I cook for castaways. Same work, less shouting.
My sister is across the water. She will be old by now, or gone. I am fifty-two, and I will stay fifty-two. So I stir the pot, and I don't think about it.
That is Biscuit, and he is a better kitchen helper than any boy I ever hired. Rats killed me once. Rats! Biscuit was not with me then. Now he is with me always.
Go well, and come back hungry, o.

onEnter.text: Where did I leave that trap...

script.text: Mind your feet. Some of what's in this grass is mine. ...Mm. Most of it, actually.

then.text: Traps. Nets on land, I call them. Rope and nails, and the wrecks bring both. Rope from your own ship, likely. Fitting, I think.
I've no trap ready to sell today. The last one I finished, I stood in. Ask me again another time.
Eleven times. Nine of them my own traps. ...Mm. I keep making them better, so it keeps hurting more. I call that progress.
Peregrine. Fisherman, born here, and sixty years on the water before the water stopped mattering. I had a wife. She died the winter before Halvard's rune, the old way, in her bed.
I think she was lucky. Her name went about my fifth death. ...Mm. Margit at the inn remembers my crew for me. Good of her.
Watch the grass. I'll be in it somewhere.

with.line: Fresh off the wreck! Lanterns and sacking!

script.text: Morning, my 'andsome! Whatever was in your hold is mine now, unless you want to buy it back. Fair's fair, I'm the one who dragged it out.

then.text: Fresh up off the wrecks, still dripping. Lanterns and a few tools, proper stuff.
A {item:hand-lantern}. Off a ship's galley, I reckon. It still lights; I tried it myself.

traded.text: Lovely! Pleasure doing business. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, my 'andsome. Somebody'll have it dreckly. Anything else?

then.text: A {item:simple-hammer}. Came out of a carpenter's chest, still oiled. Brannoc wants twenty for a new one; this one's fifteen and it's done some work already.

traded.text: Lovely! Pleasure doing business. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, my 'andsome. Somebody'll have it dreckly. Anything else?

then.text: A {item:simple-axe}. Off a ship's woodpile, a bit of rust on the cheek, nothing a stone won't sort. Fifteen gold, my 'andsome.

traded.text: Lovely! Pleasure doing business. Anything else?

cancel.text: Your loss, my 'andsome. Somebody'll have it dreckly. Anything else?

then.text: Right you are. What else?
Wenna. Shipwright's apprentice, born here. I was going to build ships, see. Nobody needs a ship that can't leave, so I take them apart. Same tools, other way round.
Drowning's the bad one. Second worst on the island, after a troll. Three times now, working the wrecks. Don't you go in after anything; leave that to me.
Bring me anything that floats, mind! I pay. Not much, but I pay.

onEnter.text: Tails, wings, bones! I'll buy them!

script.text: Oi, squire! Rat tails, bat wings, bones. I pay a little. The towns pay more, honest, but the towns are a long way off, and I'm right here, ain't I?

then.text: Go on, turn out your pockets. I won't touch. Much.
1 gold per {item:rat-tail}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:bat-wing}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:rabbit-foot}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:raccoon-tail}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:bone}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 2 gold per {item:snake-fang}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: 2 gold per {item:boar-tusk}. Robbery, I know, but it's the honest kind.

traded.text: Done and done. Anything else, squire?

cancel.text: Fair enough. Can't blame a man for asking. Anything else?

then.text: Right you are. What else, squire?
Jory Thistlewood. Harbour pickpocket, born and bred, and I'll not lie to you about it. Nobody can hang you here. I like that about the place.
Brannoc killed me four times for one stolen knife. Four! Fair, I suppose. I'm very polite to him now.
Human skull? Put that away, squire, put it away. Somebody here knew them. Even I won't sell that.
Mind your pockets. Not from me. Probably.

script.text: Welcome to the temple town, {partner}. You may carve what you like here. You may not carve it at anyone. The council is quite firm on that point.

then.text: The wolves come to the garden plots at night, and the council has set a bounty: four gold for every {item:wolf-skin} brought to this house. I pay it myself.

traded.text: Paid, and entered in the town's accounts. The plots thank you. Is there anything further?

cancel.text: As you wish. Is there anything further?

then.text: I do. I was the harbour's magistrate. When the water came in, somebody had to tell people where to walk. I told them, and they have been asking me ever since.
I am still leading them, a hundred and thirty years later. Nobody else has had the chance to try. I do not say that with pride.
Consider it as I must. Break Wyrd, and Morwen is seventy and Peregrine is sixty, and both of them are a hundred and thirty years late for their graves.
I do not say it must never be done. I say somebody should think about that before they climb.
Absalom was my captain of the watch. I still call him Captain, and he still answers to it. He took the people who refused runes east, and I let them go rather than fight.
Twelve deaths. Three of them were our own people, in the year before the split. Those are the ones I remember.
Go carefully, {partner}. This town has buried nobody in a century, and it would prefer not to start.

with.line: Bring me a blank and an essence.

script.text: Welcome to the temple, {partner}. Mind the forges; they are older than the town, and they do not care who touches them. Now. What would you like to learn?

then.text: Three forges, three materials. The first forge takes bone. The second, crystal. The third, the deep ore. Shape your blank there, and bring it here to me.
The counts matter, so listen. Three bones make a bone blank. Four crystal shards make a crystal one. Five of obsidian make the last.
Bone gives a crude rune, crystal a better one, and obsidian the strongest marks I can cut. Say it back to me next time, and I will know you listened.

options.label: How do I get a rune carved?

then.text: Bring me the blank and ask me to carve it. Ten gold for bone, thirty for crystal, sixty for obsidian. The fee is not open to discussion; Dagny will tell you she has tried.
Bring an essence with the blank and the rune takes its element: fire, water or nature. Bring none and it stays plain.
Every creature carries a little of its own element. Hunt enough of them and one will leave you its essence.
And understand this before you pay me: what the mark becomes is not up to either of us. Halvard taught me that before he taught me anything else.
Name a blank and I will tell you what it can become. Which one comes out is chance. Choose.
Bone. It takes the plainest marks, and it is where every carver begins.
With no essence, {item:rune-light} or {item:rune-spark}.
With fire, {item:rune-flame} or {item:rune-cinder}.
With water, {item:rune-sleet}.
With nature, {item:rune-barbs}.
Crystal. It holds more, and holds it longer.
With no essence, {item:rune-bolt} or {item:rune-lance}.
With fire, {item:rune-ember} or {item:rune-pyre}.
With water, {item:rune-frost} or {item:rune-rime}.
With nature, {item:rune-thorns}, {item:rune-bramble}, {item:rune-verdance} or {item:rune-bloom}.
Obsidian. It takes the strongest marks I can cut, and it cuts back if you are careless with it.
With no essence, {item:rune-stomp}.
With fire, {item:rune-inferno} or {item:rune-berserk}.
With water, {item:rune-shatter} or {item:rune-crystallise}.
With nature, {item:rune-overgrowth} or {item:rune-blossom}.
I was his pupil, one of very few. Halvard was the best carver who ever lived. I say his name because nobody else in this town will.
He cut one rune too deep, and we are all still inside it.
I remember people growing old. I don't miss it, and I would give it back tomorrow.
Seven deaths. Each time I check my hands afterwards, to see if they still know the marks.
Go well. Repeat the counts to yourself on the road: three, four, five.

with.line: Light and Spark, ready-carved!

script.text: Light and Spark are ready-carved, shelved and priced. Anything stronger, bring a blank to the runemaster. Not to me. Not yet.

then.text: Plain runes, carved by Hesper herself, entered in the book, and priced by me.
{item:rune-light}. It makes a light where you need one. Even a warrior could manage it.

traded.text: Entered in the book. Next?

cancel.text: Noted. Next?

then.text: {item:rune-spark}. A small bolt. Enough to start with. I had mine working in an afternoon, for the record.

traded.text: Entered in the book. Next?

cancel.text: Noted. Next?

then.text: Very well. What else?
The temple buys what the forges take, at the temple's prices. They are fixed, so please don't haggle.
1 gold per {item:bone}. That's the rate in the book.

traded.text: Paid and entered. Next?

cancel.text: Noted. Next?

then.text: 4 gold per {item:obsidian-shard}. That's the rate in the book.

traded.text: Paid and entered. Next?

cancel.text: Noted. Next?

then.text: Very well. What else?
Dagny Rook, temple clerk. I kept the harbour master's books before Wyrd. He was my father, and he would have hated that lighthouse, for the record.
One death in a hundred and thirty years. A bog imp. A small one. I'd rather not talk about it, and I'd be grateful if you didn't either.
The temple closes at dusk. Sharp.

with.line: Robes that hold a spell!

script.text: Come in, come in, slowly. This one holds a spell better. That one is warmer. You can't have both, my friend; cloth is like people that way.

then.text: Cloth for people who cast. Feel it, go on. Gently.
{item:cloth-tunic}. One point, and better than a shirt. A simple little thing, but I wove it slowly.

traded.text: Wear it well, and it will learn your shape. Anything else?

cancel.text: No hurry, no hurry. Anything else?

then.text: {item:tunic-of-flames}. Red from wisp ash, many dippings. It makes you a fire creature on the wheel.

traded.text: Wear it well, and it will learn your shape. Anything else?

cancel.text: No hurry, no hurry. Anything else?

then.text: {item:mantle-of-brambles}. Green from the little white moss, strange as that sounds. It makes you nature on the wheel.

traded.text: Wear it well, and it will learn your shape. Anything else?

cancel.text: No hurry, no hurry. Anything else?

then.text: Of course. What else?
Little things, to wear with a robe. Small does not mean weak.
{item:copper-ring}. One flat point, against anything. A little ring, a little help, always.

traded.text: Wear it well, and it will learn your shape. Anything else?

cancel.text: No hurry, no hurry. Anything else?

then.text: {item:amulet-of-tides}. Blue as the bay used to be. It makes you water on the wheel.

traded.text: Wear it well, and it will learn your shape. Anything else?

cancel.text: No hurry, no hurry. Anything else?

then.text: Of course. What else?
Amaru. I came from the mountains across the sea, very high, where the air is thin and the wool is good. On the harbour I wove sailcloth. My first robe here was the last bolt of it.
The frost caves killed me eight times. Eight. The little white moss I dye with is worth it. Look at this green and tell me it isn't.
Halina makes coats that stop my customers' spells. I tell her she is weaving against me. She laughs, buys me a drink, and goes on doing it.
Go slowly. Come back when it's cold.

with.line: Potions! Bottles bought!

script.text: Jelly from a slime, ash from a wisp. Not 'goo', not 'dust'. Potions to buy, bottles and spoils to sell. Separately, please.

then.text: Drink one and you glow for an hour. Exactly an hour; I timed it. Fourteen gold apiece. How many?

traded.text: Drink them somewhere dark. The effect is wasted in daylight. Anything else?

cancel.text: As you like. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold for every {item:empty-bottle}. Rinsed, please. How many have you got?

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: Slime jelly, and what a wisp leaves when it goes out: ash, dew or spore, depending on the wisp. Not 'dust'. I brew with all of it.
1 gold per {item:nature-slime-jelly}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:water-slime-jelly}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: 1 gold per {item:fire-slime-jelly}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: 3 gold per {item:wisp-ash}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: 3 gold per {item:wisp-dew}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: 3 gold per {item:wisp-spore}. Keep each kind in its own jar, please.

traded.text: Thank you. Noted. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep them, then. Anything else?

then.text: Very well. What else?
Noor Halabi. I came from abroad as a spice merchant's buyer; I could tell a cargo's worth by smell. Pell the baker is my husband. He talks, and I write things down.
Nineteen deaths, and most of them my own fault. A poison you've tasted is a poison you understand. I have the notes to prove it.
Write down what you learn, {partner}. The next death will take some of it.

with.line: Bread off a Flame rune! Pies!

script.text: Morning! Or is it afternoon? I've been up since the dark. Everything here is baked on a Flame rune, not wood, so there's no smoke in the crust, just crust. Tastes cleaner. Don't tell the warriors.

then.text: Three gold a slice, and it's a generous slice, and the apples are Suvi's, and the pastry flakes if you so much as look at it.

traded.text: Oh, enjoy it. Eat it while it's warm, the butter's still moving. Anything else?

cancel.text: No? Your loss, honestly. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold a loaf. Knock on the bottom: hear that? Hollow. That's a proper loaf.

traded.text: There you go, still warm. Anything else?

cancel.text: No? Your loss, honestly. Anything else?

then.text: One gold per {item:apple}. I need them for the pies; I go through a barrel a week.

traded.text: Lovely, lovely. Anything else?

cancel.text: No? Your loss, honestly. Anything else?

then.text: One gold per {item:berry}. They go in the honey cakes. Not if they're stale, mind!

traded.text: Oh, these are good ones. Thank you! Anything else?

cancel.text: No? Your loss, honestly. Anything else?

then.text: Pell. I baked ship's biscuit for the harbour, which is the worst thing you can do to flour, honestly. Noor at the apothecary is my wife. She eats what I bake and tells me what's in it.
Four deaths in a hundred and thirty years. I'm careful. I bake. Bakers don't die much; we stay near the oven.

A troll, on the road. First it sat on me. Then it sniffed me all over, the way I'd sniff a loaf to see if it's done. Then, well. It took a long time. I don't walk that road any more; Yeva carries my bread.
Come back when you're hungry! Or before. I don't mind.

with.line: Apples, a gold each!

script.text: Apples are a gold. Rabbit feet buy you one free.

then.text: One gold each. Pick your own. Don't squeeze them.

traded.text: There. What else?

cancel.text: Fine. What else?

then.text: One gold a handful. My hand, not yours.

traded.text: There. What else?

cancel.text: Fine. What else?

then.text: One {item:rabbit-foot} for one {item:apple}. I bury them in the plots for luck.

traded.text: That's luck for a row. Anything else?

cancel.text: Fine. What else?

then.text: Suvi. I came from the cold north as a fisherman's wife. He drowned long before Wyrd.
I haven't eaten a fish in a hundred years. Good.
The wolves come out of the woods at night. Five times now. They take the throat first, if you want to know.
Mind the rows.

script.text: Evening, young one. The lamps don't light themselves. Well. They nearly do, these days, but don't tell anyone.

then.text: I light every lamp in town at dusk with a flick of a Spark rune, like so, and put them out at dawn. Fifty years with a taper, and now it's a flick. I'm a lucky old man.
Tobiah over in the warriors' town uses a taper. I taught him that. I've learned better since. He'll tell you different. He's wrong, bless him.
Casimir Wren. I came here as a ship's boy, no taller than that barrel, and lit the harbour lamps for fifty years. Somebody had to keep the quay bright.
I lit the quay the night Wyrd took hold. I'd just reached the last lamp when I looked up, and the lighthouse went from yellow to white. I've not cared for white light since.
The light on the lighthouse is the only lamp on this island I'd put out if I could.
Stay where it's lit, young one. That's what I'm for.

with.line: A gold for every rat tail!

script.text: Oh! Hello. Have you died yet? Here, I mean? What was it like? Everyone says it's bad, but nobody says how bad, or what kind of bad, do you see?

then.text: Two gold a loaf, from my own flour. Is that all right? Pell says it's the best flour on the island, but he's kind.

traded.text: There. Was that the right change? Anything else?

cancel.text: Oh. That's all right. Anything else?

then.text: I pay a bounty on rats, did you know? One gold a tail. Soot can't catch all of them. Can you, Soot?

traded.text: One fewer rat! Thank you. Anything else?

cancel.text: Oh. That's all right. Anything else?

then.text: Mina. The miller's wife. Still, I suppose? My husband went across the sea to buy millstones a month before Wyrd. He hasn't come back. Nothing comes back, does it?
Did you come from across the water? Is there a man there who sells millstones? Is he old? Is he... is he well?
Me? Not once. A hundred and thirty years. Isn't that strange? I keep thinking it is going to be today. Do you think it will hurt very much?
Soot does the rats. Soot is the black one. He's never died either. Do cats?
Be careful out there. Will you? Promise?

script.text: Sit down. Tell me how it happened. Slowly, please. I'll read it back to you.

then.text: You have an entry already. Volume forty, near the end. Come and read it after the next time.

else.text: There. Your name. The day. What you tell me you've lost. I'll read it back: is that right? Good.
Next time you wake, come and read it.

then.text: Anyone may tell me how they died and what they lost. I write it down, so after the next death they can read what they no longer remember.
It is forty volumes now. I began it the year I found I couldn't remember my mother's face.
Rosalind. I was a copyist in the harbour's counting houses. Anselm the pilgrim is my brother. He walks, and I write.
Twenty-eight deaths. I have read about every one of them, and remember almost none.
I have the entries of everyone who has climbed to Maren. They're short. They get shorter.
Come back and read it.

with.line: Mind the scaffolding!

script.text: Now then. I grow the timber, and then I build with it. The growing takes a while. I've the time.

then.text: Orrin. Mason, born here, and my father before me. The two of us laid the lower floors of Halvard's lighthouse, stone by stone, one long summer.
I didn't know what it would be for. Nobody did. I think about that more than I'd like.
Maren used to bring us bread and sit on the stones while we ate. She laughed a lot. I'd rather remember her like that.
People died of age here, once. My father did, the year before, in his chair with his boots on. I've died sixteen times since. Roofs had half of them. You'd think I'd learn.
Mind the scaffolding.

with.line: Have I told you about Maren?

script.text: Have I told you about Maren? I've told someone. Probably you. Have I? Well, it's worth hearing twice.

then.text: You can't climb it alone. That's the first thing. The upper floors need four of you, and four who trust each other. Four. Did I say four? Four.
She doesn't speak. She looks at you as if she is trying to remember your name. I know how that is.
Did I give you something? I'm sure I did. Did I? Good. Good.

else.text: I've an old sword here I don't need. I don't remember why I have it. There's a nick in the blade. I don't remember that either.

traded.text: Take it. I won't remember giving it to you.

cancel.text: Keep it in mind, then. One of us should.

then.text: Fen. I was a deckhand, Tove says. I rowed in her whaleboat. She'd know. I believe her.
Three hundred and some deaths. I lost count, and then I lost the count.
Oh, before you go. Have I told you about Maren?

onEnter.text: Hey {traveller}, don't stray too far south. The woods bite.

script.text: Temple's open, {partner}. Forges are inside, the runemaster's at the back.

then.text: Taavi, day warden. I was in the harbour watch under Absalom. I chose the runes; he chose the drill yard.
Twenty-seven deaths. Two of those were Absalom. He was right to; it was a bad year.
Inside the town, yes. Wolves come out of the deep woods, and bog imps from the west. I go after both. If you hear a howl, come inside.
The temple's the middle of town. The four streets run from it to the four gates.
Dagny sells them at the desk inside, by the steps. Hesper carves them at the back, between the forges.
Amaru's weaving house. East side of the square, over the little bridge.
Noor's apothecary, south of the square, on the east side of the street.
Pell's bakehouse is across the street from the apothecary. Suvi sells apples at the garden plots, in the south-west corner.

options.label: A place to keep my things

then.text: The depot, west of the square, past the wardens' house. Every chest there opens on your own things, and nobody else sees them.
The council house, west side of the square. Iolanthe hears people there.
Keep to the road.

with.line: Stay under the lamps.

script.text: Late to be walking. Stay under the lamps; that's what they're for.

then.text: Nadia, night warden. I came from abroad as a sailor and worked the harbour's night boats. Middle watch, every night. I never got the habit of sleeping in the dark back.
I carry my own light. Casimir says it makes his lamps look bad. I tell him that's the idea.
The wolves come to the plots after midnight. Eighteen deaths, and they were half of them.
Stay lit.

with.line: Your things are safe here. Come and see.

script.text: Welcome to the depot, {partner}. The chests along the back wall are yours.

then.text: Open any chest here and you see your own things, nobody else's. Put something in, and it is waiting for you the next time you open any of them.
Three chests, one store. Use whichever is free; the stranger at the next one sees only theirs.
Death takes your bag. It does not take what you left here. Most people come straight back to this counter after.
Nothing. Bread you leave today is bread in a hundred years. I would know.
Not on this island. If you want something kept, bring it here.
Mirela Dobos. Before Wyrd I kept the bonded warehouse on the harbour: every crate that came off a ship sat with me until its duty was paid.
The warehouse never shut, so I never learned to. I don't sleep here either. Somebody always wants their things at three in the morning.
Mind your bag on the road.

with.line: Want the tower? Nobody climbs it alone. Talk to me.

script.text: Ha! You've got the look. You want the tower? Good! You can't climb it alone, mind. Nobody can. Nobody!

then.text: You're on my list already, {partner}! I don't forget a name. I'll find you three more, don't you worry.

else.text: Done! Your name's on the list. Give me time, and I'll find you three more. Three good ones.

then.text: I do! Absalom brought us here, and I built the walls. We each did the part we were good at, and nobody argued. Much.
I ran the harbour's ropewalk before Wyrd. Forty people, all pulling the same way. One strand is nothing; forty is a rope. This town is easier.
Eleven times on the tower! And every one of them because somebody behind me ran. So now I pick who stands behind me.
Iolanthe thinks we should wait and see what breaking it does. Ha! I've waited a hundred and thirty years. I've seen.
Train! Then come back, and we'll see.

with.line: Up at dawn! Train it!

script.text: Stand straight. Up at dawn. A body is the one thing on this island no rune made. Train it.

then.text: Absalom Grieve. Formerly captain of the harbour watch. I led the people who refused runes east. Ragna runs the town. I run the drill. That is the arrangement.
Forty-four deaths. I learn something every time. Mostly what not to do.
Break the rune at the top of the tower and we all go back to dying once. That seems right to me.
The druids are not wicked. They are using the same knife that cut us.
Dawn. Drill yard. Do not be late.

with.line: Swords! Axes! Don't touch the hot ones.

script.text: Hm. Swords there. Axes there. Don't touch the hot ones.

then.text: Blades. Twenty for the plain one, fifty for a knight's, ninety-five for the tempered.
{item:iron-sword}. Straight, quick, asks Sharp 6 of you.

traded.text: Keep the edge off the stone. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: {item:knights-sword}. Truer than the iron and slower with it — Sharp 20.

traded.text: That one has a name where it came from. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Folded and quenched twice. Sharp 34, and worth every point of it.

traded.text: Best blade on the rack, and you know it. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Suit yourself. What else?
Axes, then. They land wilder than a blade and they land harder.
A woodsman's axe. Sharp 8, and it swings like a chore.

traded.text: Mind your shins. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: {item:broad-axe} — a hand's width of edge. Sharp 20 and Toughness 8 to hold it up.

traded.text: Heavy at the head, that's the point of it. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Two bits, two hands. Sharp 34 and Toughness 16, and nothing stands after it.

traded.text: You'll need both hands and both feet. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Fair enough. What else?
Blunt work. Nothing clever about it, and it never turns on the bone.
My own pattern. Blunt 5, and it does the same thing every time.

traded.text: It'll not surprise you. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Flanged head, iron through. Blunt 18.

traded.text: That'll dent a helm. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Both hands. Blunt 32 and Toughness 16 — it's more weight than weapon.

traded.text: Swing it once and mean it. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Right you are. What else?
Shields. A shield is held, so it costs you a hand and pays you back on every blow.
A {item:buckler}. One point of defence and it weighs nothing.

traded.text: Small, but it's there. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Boards and a rim. Two points, off every blow that lands.

traded.text: It'll split before you do. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Three points. Carry one in each hand if you like — they add.

traded.text: Now let them come. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Please yourself. What else?
A gold for every {item:bone}. It goes in the quench. How many?

traded.text: Good. What else?

cancel.text: Suit yourself. Anything else?

then.text: Brannoc. Harpoons and anchor chain, for the harbour. Tove the hunter is my sister. Hm. Younger.
Iron doesn't care what you believe. That's why I like it.
Come back when you've something to spend, {partner}.

with.line: Bows! If you can see it, you can hit it.

script.text: If you can see it, you can hit it. Most of the time. Want to bet on which time this is?

then.text: Reach is what you're paying for. The further off it is, the less it bites.
Two cells out to six, and a prayer. Ranged 5.

traded.text: Good. Now go and beat my count. Anything else?

cancel.text: Scared of it? Fine. Anything else?

then.text: Two out to eight. Ranged 18. I took a deer at seven with this one, through brush.

traded.text: Good. Now go and beat my count. Anything else?

cancel.text: Scared of it? Fine. Anything else?

then.text: Two out to ten, and a heavier arrow at the end of them. Ranged 32. Nobody in town draws it clean but me. Yet.

traded.text: Good. Now go and beat my count. Anything else?

cancel.text: Scared of it? Fine. Anything else?

then.text: Fine. What else?
Selin. I came from a horse country across the sea as a merchant's guard, and stayed.
A cyclops, three times in a week. The third time I nearly had it. Nearly. There'll be a fourth.
Mateo says start with a spear. Mateo is wrong. Ask him how many cyclopes he's shot. Go on, ask him.
Aim low. They duck.

with.line: Old weapons bought! Something for anything!

script.text: Hey! Old sword? Old axe? I'll give you something for it. Not much! But something. That's my whole business, friend.

then.text: Go on, what are you getting rid of? Don't tell me it's good. Everybody says it's good.
8 gold per {item:iron-sword}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 8 gold per {item:simple-axe}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 8 gold per {item:simple-hammer}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 8 gold per {item:simple-bow}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold per {item:knights-sword}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold per {item:broad-axe}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold per {item:iron-mace}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold per {item:hunting-bow}. Too little? It's used! Somebody died holding it. Probably you.

traded.text: Done! You robbed me. Anything else?

cancel.text: Ay, you wound me. Fine. Anything else?

then.text: Right, right. What else?
Mateo! I came from abroad as a sailor, from... the word's gone. Somewhere warm. Then I joined the harbour watch.
I used to dream in another language. Lost it about my twentieth death. Now I dream in this one, and the dreams are worse.
A spear keeps them a step away. Out here a step is everything. Don't listen to Selin. I'm out of spears today, mind.
Keep your edge! And when you don't, bring it to me.

with.line: Armour that makes a spell miss!

script.text: This coat takes a fire spell and gives back half of it as heat. You'll be warm and alive. I've tested both, personally.

then.text: Body first — it is the piece that is hit. Every point comes off every blow that lands.
{item:warded-robe}. One point, and six against anything arcane.

traded.text: Let them throw fire at you. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:padded-gambeson}. Two points, and four more against blunt.

traded.text: A club will not find much in that. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:leather-jerkin}. Two points, and two each against sharp blows and arrows.

traded.text: Turns a point better than it turns a hammer. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:chain-mail}. Three points, and four more against sharp blows.

traded.text: Rings turn an edge. They do nothing for a maul. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:steel-plate}. Five points, three each against sharp blows and arrows. The best I have.

traded.text: Now let them try. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: Right. What else?
Charms. None of them is armour and every one of them is defence — read the numbers.
{item:bone-charm}. Four against a fist or a jaw, and nothing else.

traded.text: Wolves hate it. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:jade-amulet}. Five against the arcane.

traded.text: Against a spell, nothing better this side of the robe. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: Your call. Come back after something hits you. What else?
Halina. I came from abroad and ran a sailmaker's loft. I learned what stops a spell by having spells cast at me.
Six times the druids burned me to test a lining. I paid them for it. Best money I ever spent.
Come back before something bites you, {partner}, not after.

with.line: Smoked meat! Eat before the waste!

script.text: Raw meat in, smoked meat out! And shut that door, you're letting my smoke out.

then.text: Three gold a slab. Smoked all day over oak, and you'll taste every hour of it.

traded.text: There. Eat it, don't just carry it about. Anything else?

cancel.text: Hmph. That's your stomach's business. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold. Good hard cheese; it keeps a month in a pack.

traded.text: There. Eat it, don't just carry it about. Anything else?

cancel.text: Hmph. That's your stomach's business. Anything else?

then.text: One gold a cut. Fresh, mind. If it's gone green, take it back outside.

traded.text: Into the smoke it goes. Anything else?

cancel.text: Hmph. That's your stomach's business. Anything else?

then.text: Bertha. I came from abroad as a ship's provisioner. I fed the ships, and now I feed a town.
And I'll tell you what I tell everyone: eat before you go into the waste. A full belly mends you on the way. An empty one gets you carried back.
A troll. It held me down and took its time. Ask anyone. Nothing worse.
Eat something first! I mean it.

with.line: Claws, tusks, furs! I buy the lot!

script.text: Bear claw, troll tusk, yeti fur. Whatever you killed, I'll buy a piece. As long as it stays dead.

then.text: Let's see it. Lay it on the bench. If it twitches, tell me first.
2 gold per {item:snake-fang}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 3 gold per {item:imp-horn}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 5 gold per {item:bear-claw}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 6 gold per {item:troll-tusk}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 8 gold per {item:skull-troll}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 20 gold per {item:yeti-fur}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: 25 gold per {item:cyclops-eye}. Cleaner than my old trade, and the goods don't get up and walk off.

traded.text: Done. Rest in pieces. Anything else?

cancel.text: Keep it, then. It won't keep long. Anything else?

then.text: Right. What else?
Animal skulls, yes. That's a person's skull? Take it back to where they woke up and give it to them. They'll want it.
Magda. I kept a saddlery with Idris, and dug up the dead on the side. Then the dead stopped staying put.
Seven deaths. Twice to bears I was skinning that were not as dead as I thought. I check three times now.
Bring me something big. And dead. Properly dead.

script.text: Every lamp in this town lit with a real flame! By hand! Mine!

then.text: I light the lamps at dusk with a taper from the smithy, and put them out at dawn. Casimir uses a rune. Cheat. Don't tell him I said that. Actually, do.
Tobiah. I was Casimir's apprentice on the quay, and a junior in the watch.
A hundred and thirty years and I still look nineteen. Nobody takes me seriously.
Fell off a lamp post twice. Woke up at the bottom of it both times. Saved me the climb down!
Mind the lamp posts. They're taller than they look.

with.line: Rope, flint, torches!

script.text: Good day, and thank you for coming in. Rope, flint, oil, torches. Everything you need and nothing you don't.

then.text: Counted, labelled, and on the shelf. Counted twice, in fact.
A {item:hand-lantern}. You can't go about in the dark without one.

traded.text: Thank you kindly. That's one off the count. Anything else?

cancel.text: Of course. It stays on the count. Anything else?

then.text: A {item:sack}. It holds what you put in it and nothing else, which is all a sack should do.

traded.text: Thank you kindly. That's one off the count. Anything else?

cancel.text: Of course. It stays on the count. Anything else?

then.text: Certainly. What else?
Rukmini. I kept a ship's chandlery on the harbour. I came here because I trust what I can count.
Two deaths, both wolves, both on the road. I don't walk it now.
That's Ghee. He caught nine rats last week, fourteen the week before. He gets a share of the bounty, paid in cream.
Count your change. I always do.

onEnter.text: Hey {traveller}, don't stray too far north. Not yet.

then.text: No runes past this gate, {partner}. And don't go far into the waste yet.

else.text: No runes past this gate, {partner}. Not in your pack, not in your pocket.

then.text: I was born on this island. I watched it stop. One man and one rune did that.
Edda. I kept Halvard's door and the lighthouse stores. Absalom is my brother.
Hesper and I were friends. She still carves. So, no.
Fifty-three. You stop counting what it takes. You start counting what's left.
Keep the wall in sight.

script.text: Barrels, buckets and charcoal. Nothing that bursts.

then.text: Aurelio. A ship's carpenter who settled, and then the temple's best carver after Hesper.
A rune I shaped burst in my hand and burned a woman at the forge. She woke. I left that week. ...Forgive me. I don't usually say so much.
I can still tell you how a mark is cut. I can't do it any more. I'm glad.
The druids aren't wrong. I just found out I couldn't be trusted with it.
Barrels don't burst.

with.line: Keep your feet under you!

script.text: Keep your feet under you. It's the only thing out there you can trust.

then.text: Nine trolls. Every one of them took longer than you'd think.
Bear caves, deep in the Greenwood. Don't go in alone, and don't go in hungry.
Sigrun. I was a lookout on the harbour wall. Then I hunted trolls, until the ninth.
They say you get used to dying. You don't. You just get used to being afraid.
Feet under you.

with.line: Waste is quiet today. That means nothing.

script.text: Mm-mm-hmm. Waste is quiet today. That means nothing.

then.text: The Red Waste. Small things burn at the edge; worse things further in; the gorge is worst.
Now and then a troll comes up out of the gorge. Six of my deaths were trolls.
Gideon. I came from abroad as a stevedore and worked Ragna's ropewalk.
Forty-one deaths. You never stop hearing the troll ones.
Selin shoots past my ear. She hasn't hit me yet. Twice. Ha!
Keep the gate behind you. I'll be singing. If I stop, run.

script.text: Who's that? Oh. Go on, then.

then.text: Liv, night watch. I was an apprentice in Halina's sail loft. I came east because she did.
Fifteen. Three of them were the walls. Watch your step up here.
From up here you can see the light on the lighthouse all night. I don't look at it much.
Mind the dark.

with.line: Ale's three gold! Fight outside!

script.text: Come in out of the weather, {partner}, love. Ale's three gold a mug. Fight outside.

then.text: How many mugs, love? Kofi brews it out back.

traded.text: There you are, love. Anything else?

cancel.text: Suit yourself, love. Anything else?

then.text: Bertha's smoked meat. Three gold. Better than anything I'd cook.

traded.text: There you are, love. Anything else?

cancel.text: Suit yourself, love. Anything else?

then.text: Pell's bread. Two gold. Yeva brings it every morning, still warm if she's quick.

traded.text: There you are, love. Anything else?

cancel.text: Suit yourself, love. Anything else?

then.text: Margit. I fished from Peregrine's boat and kept his accounts. I built this place so both towns could drink in one room.
A hundred and thirty years, and I've buried nobody. I've just watched them all come back through that door.
Druids at that end, warriors at this end. Everybody drinks the same ale.
Mind how you go, {partner}.

with.line: Best ale on the island!

script.text: Best ale on the island. Only ale on the island, but still.

then.text: Three gold a mug. I'd do you a discount, but then it wouldn't be the best ale on the island, would it?

traded.text: Cheers! Anything else?

cancel.text: No? More for me, then. Anything else?

then.text: One gold a handful. They go in the brew.

traded.text: Done. Into the pot. Anything else?

cancel.text: No? More for me, then. Anything else?

then.text: One gold a cut, for the stew.

traded.text: Done. Into the pot. Anything else?

cancel.text: No? More for me, then. Anything else?

then.text: Kofi. Cabin hand, then a cook in Ifeoma's kitchen. I brewed the first ale after the harbour's breweries flooded.
Eleven deaths. A wolf at the door, last. At the door!
Don't let the druids heat your ale.

script.text: Buy me an ale and I'll tell you how I got past the first floor. Hic.

then.text: Fen and I went up together, the two of us and two more whose names... no. Gone. Four of you, or don't go. Hic.
Maren looked at me. Like she knew me, and was sorry. That was the worst of it. Not the dying.
A hundred and sixty. I used to mark every map with a little cross where it happened. Bless them, every little cross.
Rodrigo. I fished for Peregrine. Nobody needed fish after the harbour went, so I went into the caves. Hic.
Shame. Still, to your health, friend. Hic.

with.line: No runes in this house.

script.text: No runes in this house, child. Wipe your feet. Both of them.

then.text: Bog root and honey, boiled the old way. It mends you, as it mended folk before ever a rune was cut. Ten gold.

traded.text: Drink it slow. Anything more, child?

cancel.text: As you please. Anything more?

then.text: What did the bog give you? She gives, you know, as well as takes.
2 gold per {item:blue-mushroom}. The bog will want it back one day, mind.

traded.text: Done. Anything more?

cancel.text: As you please. Anything more?

then.text: 3 gold per {item:imp-horn}. The bog will want it back one day, mind.

traded.text: Done. Anything more?

cancel.text: As you please. Anything more?

then.text: Well then. What else?
I sat with Maren while she went. She went well. Then he brought her back.
Thirty times the bog has had me. It gives me back every time, a bit less.
On a still night you can hear her from here, up in the tower. She sings. She doesn't know the words.
Mind the boards. Some are rotten.

with.line: Which ship was yours? I'll pray for her.

script.text: Which ship was yours, {partner}? I'll pray for her. Every name goes in the prayer.

then.text: I've blessed you already. It doesn't wear off.

else.text: Bread for the road, and a blessing with it. Bow your head if you like. It works either way.

traded.text: May the road be kind to you. Go in peace.

cancel.text: The blessing stands, bread or no bread. Keep it in mind.

then.text: Anselm. I was lay brother of the harbour chapel. The chapel flooded, so the whole island is my chapel now.
Sixty times on these roads. I keep walking them.
I married Halvard and Maren, in the old chapel. Somebody should pray for her. She's had nobody but him.
Walk safely. I'll say your name at the next stop.

onEnter.text: Bread! Cheese! Lanterns! Wolves hunt at night, so buy a lantern!
Idris at the camp trades leather for skins!
Bog imps sleep round their fires at night. Go round!
Ale and a bed at Margit's inn, halfway down the road!

script.text: Ah, a new face! Bread from the druids, cheese from the warriors. Same price either way, and I tell nobody which way you bought.

then.text: Two gold. Pell's own, though between you and me, Mina's flour is half the reason.

traded.text: A pleasure, my friend. Anything else?

cancel.text: No offence taken, none at all. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold. Pell's own, though between you and me, Mina's flour is half the reason.

traded.text: A pleasure, my friend. Anything else?

cancel.text: No offence taken, none at all. Anything else?

then.text: Three gold. Wenna sells the same, but she won't walk it to you, will she?

traded.text: A pleasure, my friend. Anything else?

cancel.text: No offence taken, none at all. Anything else?

then.text: Hamid. I kept a stall on the quay. On the road I belong to neither town, and I sell to both. Each of them thinks I'm on its side. Between us, I am.
Twenty-five deaths, all on this road. There's a bend after the lake. Walk wide.
Walk wide at the bend. And if you hear anything interesting, tell me first.

with.line: Letters! Parcels!

script.text: Letter for the druids? Give it here, quick, I'm going that way. I'm always going that way.

then.text: Yeva! Came on a mail packet, ran messages for the harbour master, still running. Sorry, I can't stand still, the legs won't let me.
A troll caught me on the road once. I've run faster ever since.
Pell's bread to the inn, Rukmini's letters to Mina, and whatever you pay me to carry. Mostly bread.
A hundred and thirty years and my legs still think they're twenty-two. That part I don't mind.
Got to run! Bye!

name: Flame
description: Bone, carved with a rising flame. Kindles a fire where you point it.

name: Ember
description: Red crystal, carved with a diamond. Hurls a burning ember.

name: Frost
description: Blue crystal, carved with a cross of frost. Chills whatever it strikes.

name: Thorns
description: Green crystal, carved with a rising thorn. Strikes with a poisoned thorn.

name: Pyre
description: Red crystal, carved with a flame over logs. Bursts into fire around its target.

name: Rime
description: Blue crystal, carved with a saltire. Frosts everything around its target.

name: Bramble
description: Green crystal, carved with a tangle of stems. Grows poison briars around its target.

name: Verdance
description: Green crystal, carved with a sprouting shoot. Mends your wounds.

name: Bloom
description: Green crystal, carved with an opening bud. Heals you and draws out burns, chills and poison.

name: Cinder
description: Bone, carved with falling sparks. Flicks a cinder at a foe.

name: Sleet
description: Bone, scored with slanting rain. Flings a shard of sleet.

name: Barbs
description: Bone, carved with a barbed stem. Looses a hooked barb.

name: Light
description: Bone, carved with a beam. Makes your skin shine in the dark.

name: Spark
description: Bone, carved with a small cross. Snaps a spark of raw arcana at a foe.

name: Bolt
description: Lavender crystal, carved with a zigzag. Hurls a bolt of raw arcana.

name: Lance
description: Lavender crystal, carved with a spear. Drives a lance of raw arcana into a foe.

name: Inferno
description: Obsidian, carved with a blazing star. Sets everything around you alight.

name: Shatter
description: Obsidian, cut with a jagged crack. Bursts into ice around you.

name: Overgrowth
description: Obsidian, carved with a branching trident. Bursts into poison growth around you.

name: Stomp
description: Obsidian, carved with a blow on the ground. Shakes the earth and dazes everyone around you.

name: Berserk
description: Obsidian, carved with bared teeth. Fills you with a careless fury.

name: Crystallise
description: Obsidian, carved with a cold diamond. Cases you in ice.

name: Blossom
description: Obsidian, carved with two linked buds. You flower and mend fast.

particles.offsetX: 0.7 * (1 - 0.5 * LIFE) * cos(9 * AGE_SEC + PI * floor(2 * SEED))
particles.offsetY: 0.7 * (1 - 0.5 * LIFE) * sin(9 * AGE_SEC + PI * floor(2 * SEED))

name: Blank Arcane Stone
description: An uncut stone. The stone forge can shape it into a rune.

name: Climbing ivy (tall, wall to the north)
Climbing ivy (tall, wall to the west)
Bone Blank
description: Bone shaped for carving. Only the runemaster can cut a mark into it.

name: Crystal Blank
description: Crystal shaped for carving. It stays clear until an essence colours it.

name: Obsidian Blank
description: Obsidian shaped for carving. No material holds a stronger rune.

name: Fire Essence
description: A spark of fire, gathered from a creature of flame.

name: Water Essence
description: A spark of water, gathered from a creature of the tide.

name: Nature Essence
description: A spark of nature, gathered from a creature of the wild.

name: Rat Tail
description: Bald and pink, off a rat. The tanner buys them.

name: Bat Wing
description: Skin stretched over fingers, off a bat. The tanner buys them.

name: Rabbit's Foot
description: Soft, and lucky for somebody other than the rabbit. The tanner buys them.

name: Snake Fang
description: Hollow, with venom still in it. The tanner buys them.

name: Imp Horn
description: A twisted horn, off a bog imp. The tanner buys them.

name: Bear Claw
description: As long as a finger, and sharper. The tanner buys them.

name: Troll Tusk
description: Yellowed ivory, off a cave troll. The tanner buys them.

name: Yeti Fur
description: A white tuft that never gets wet. The tanner buys them.

name: Cyclops Eye
description: Still looking at you. The tanner buys them.

name: Slime Jelly
description: Green, and it wobbles. The potion seller buys it.

name: Water Slime Jelly
description: Blue, and cold to hold. The potion seller buys it.

name: Fire Slime Jelly
description: Red, and warm to hold. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Ash
description: What is left of an ember wisp. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Dew
description: What is left of a tide wisp. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Spore
description: What is left of a moss wisp. The potion seller buys it.

script.text: Stay near the fire, {partner}. Anything with teeth that comes this close gets an arrow.

then.text: Runa. I walked off a wreck like you, three winters back. Tove put a bow in my hands.

options.label: How do I get better with a bow?

then.text: Shoot rats. Then shoot more rats. Keep two cells between you and whatever you shoot.
You've got it already. That was my only spare. Selin in the warriors' town sells new ones.

else.text: The one I learned on. It's yours for ten gold. Take it after the deer and rabbits round the camp: they run, they don't bite back, and you'll learn your distance.

traded.text: Look after it. Two cells back, and let the rabbit come to you.

cancel.text: It'll be here. Nobody else wants it.

then.text: Keep the fire in sight.

name: Boar Tusk
description: Curved, and sharp at the tip, off a boar. The tanner buys them.

name: Raccoon Tail
description: Ringed grey and black, off a raccoon. The tanner buys them.
